answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost. A relic stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a opal hold...
